title: Maximize Grid Happiness
summary: Given m, n, introvertsCount, and extrovertsCount, place people in an m x n grid to maximize the grid happiness.
statement: Given m, n, introvertsCount, and extrovertsCount, place people in an m x n grid to maximize the grid happiness. Each introvert starts with 120 happiness and loses 30 for each neighbor. Each extrovert starts with 40 happiness and gains 20 for each neighbor. Neighbors are directly adjacent cells. The grid happiness is the total happiness of all people. Determine the maximum possible grid happiness.
constraints: 1 <= m,n <= 5 and each people count is between zero and six.
An introvert contributes 120 base happiness and loses 30 per occupied neighbor; an extrovert contributes 40 and gains 20 per occupied neighbor.
Place at most the supplied people to maximize total happiness.
hints: A row’s ternary digits encode empty, introvert, or extrovert cells.
Precompute each row’s internal score and every adjacent-row interaction score.
DP by row, previous row state, and counts of each personality already used.
All effects are local to horizontal neighbors in the row and vertical neighbors in the preceding row, so the compressed state retains every fact needed for future scoring.
editorial: All effects are local to horizontal neighbors in the row and vertical neighbors in the preceding row, so the compressed state retains every fact needed for future scoring.

tests.explanation: One optimal placement separates the introvert while the two extroverts benefit from adjacency, totaling 240.
Only one person fits; choosing the introvert gives 120 rather than the extrovert’s 40.
